piezas.titular: A tool turns a mobile phone and VR headset into a virtual camera for Blender
piezas.entradilla: Raül Torres describes how, with help from Claude, he built a system that records real camera movements in Blender to then guide an AI video generator.
cuerpo: Raül Torres says he has used Claude to create a tool for controlling the camera in 3D scenes without relying only on the text of a prompt. The phone version consists of a web page using WebXR that reads the phone’s position and rotation, and a Python add-on for Blender that moves the scene’s camera in real time. When he presses REC and walks around the room, Blender records the keyframes; the phone screen shows what the camera sees.

Afterwards, according to his account, the recording is stopped, an MP4 is exported and that video serves as a camera reference for the Seedance 2.5 video generator. The [official Seedance 2.5 page](https://seed.bytedance.com/en/seedance2_5) confirms that the model can take a reference video as a guide for camera movement.

A second version brings the same method to a Meta Quest 3 headset: using Quest Link and the [VR Scene Inspection](https://docs.blender.org/manual/en/latest/addons/vr_scene_inspection.html) (OpenXR) add-on that comes with Blender, the person recording holds a virtual camera in the controller, the trigger starts and stops recording, and the joysticks allow tracking shots and pans. The author notes that he still has to fine-tune details, such as the speed of the left controller.

For the audiovisual or art classroom, the idea matters because it hands control of framing and movement back to students: they build the set, decide where the camera goes and AI is used afterwards to transform that material. The author gives his own series, “Never Sleep Again”, as an example of his way of working, which [the paper reported on 1 November](pieza:2026-10-31/webserie-never-sleep-again). The tools described are a personal development and, for now, the group has only his screenshots, test videos and explanation to go on.

fuentes.titulo: Blender: VR Scene Inspection add-on manual

piezas.comprobado: Contrastado con los mensajes #12067-#12108 del grupo (WebFetch del #12067 en Telegram: es de Raül Torres, 4 nov). No hay página pública de la herramienta. El manual de Blender: el enlace del borrador daba 404; la dirección corregida abre el manual (Blender 5.2) con la página VR Scene Inspection, y la búsqueda confirma que es un complemento oficial incluido en Blender, basado en OpenXR y con seguimiento de mandos; Quest Link no aparece en el manual y se atribuye al autor. Seedance 2.5 no confirmado en fuente oficial (solo guías de terceros sobre Seedance 2.0, que sí admite vídeo de referencia de cámara): se mantiene como afirmación del autor. Se quitó la frase que atribuía al mismo autor la webserie, porque no se ha verificado.
piezas.ilustracion: Esquema en tres pasos de izquierda a derecha: un móvil o unas gafas de realidad virtual que se mueven por una habitación, una escena 3D de Blender con una cámara que sigue ese movimiento dibujada como trayectoria punteada, y un fotograma de vídeo final generado por IA a partir del recorrido.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: Three-step diagram from left to right: a phone with a red dot and the label REC, under the caption “Phone or headset”; an arrow to a 3D cube with a camera at the end of a dotted path, under the caption “Blender scene”; and another arrow to a video frame with a landscape, under the caption “AI video”.

piezas.titular: An open project offers 54 interactive 3D science lessons for upper secondary school, in Chinese
piezas.entradilla: Tongjiang Lab brings together physics, chemistry, biology and geography lessons in HTML files that work offline; in the group it was pointed to as an example of what will be possible with AI.
cuerpo: [Tongjiang Lab](https://github.com/smithjohn78390/tongjiang-lab) (铜匠实验室), an open repository of 3D science lessons for upper secondary school, was shared in Vibe Coding Educativo. According to its documentation, it contains 54 lessons: 10 in physics, 25 in chemistry, 5 in biology and 14 in geography. Each is a single HTML file of roughly 1 MB that works offline, so it can be used on a projector or an interactive whiteboard.

Each lesson presents a 3D scene with a live control panel, a guiding question and a step-by-step route for teachers. They can be opened online, downloaded one by one or as a zip, and embedded in another website via an iframe. The lessons follow the Chinese curriculum and the textbooks of the publisher People’s Education Press, although the project makes clear it has no connection with it.

The interface is in Chinese; the project says other languages are planned. The licence is CC BY-NC 4.0, which allows sharing and adapting with credit and without commercial use. The author is listed as Tongjiang.

The person who shared it in the group presents it as a sample of what will be possible in the coming months with AI, and has translated one of the simulations into English on their own website. The interest for Spanish-speaking teachers is twofold: a model of a self-contained 3D lesson and a reusable base, as long as the licence is respected.
piezas.comprobado: Abiertos el repositorio de GitHub y lab.tongjiang.app: 54 lecciones (10 física, 25 química, 5 biología, 14 geografía), HTML autocontenido de ~1 MB que funciona sin conexión, zip/descarga individual/iframe, CC BY-NC 4.0 (three.js bajo MIT), interfaz en chino con otros idiomas previstos, currículo nacional y libros PEP 2019 sin afiliación, autor Tongjiang. Abierta eduvers.org/en/simulations: solo una simulación figura en inglés, el resto bajo “Chinese”. Mensaje #14628 abierto en Telegram: coincide.
piezas.ilustracion_alt: A bar divided into four sections of proportional width, under the label “54 lessons”; above each section an icon: an atom over “Physics”, a flask over “Chemistry” (the longest section, in blue), a DNA helix over “Biology” (the shortest) and a globe over “Geography”.
piezas.correccion: Update on 13 November 2026: the project’s repository and website are no longer available. Copies remain on the Internet Archive’s Wayback Machine: [the repository](https://web.archive.org/web/20261102164409/https://github.com/smithjohn78390/tongjiang-lab) and [the lessons website](https://web.archive.org/web/20261030005733/https://lab.tongjiang.app/).

breves.texto: Raül Torres shared in EduMedia-IAG a video-game-style walk through Girona made with Claude, with places taken from the real map and time travel from the Palaeolithic to 2026. It runs from the web and no public link is available.
